You finish the weekly inventory report at 4pm on Friday. Before it goes out, you check the key figures by hand one more time.

This is the routine for a lot of operations teams. The numbers are there in the dashboard, but nobody fully trusts them until someone has looked at them side by side with the order records and the stock counts.

That gap between what the report says and what you believe is a data quality problem sitting right in operations. It is not an IT ticket to file. It is time out of your week and a delay on every decision that depends on those numbers.

In a survey of 120 operations leaders, 62% said they did not fully trust the inventory figures in their weekly report.

Think about the last report you had to verify by hand before sending it out. What did you check?

variants.hook: How much of your week goes into checking numbers you should be able to trust?
variants.body:
How much of your week goes into checking numbers you should be able to trust?

If you run operations for a mid-sized logistics or distribution business, you know the feeling. The weekly report is technically ready, but before anyone senior acts on it, someone still has to reconcile the inventory figures against the order and shipment records by hand.

That is a data quality problem. And it sits squarely in operations, not in the IT department. It shows up as hours spent on manual reconciliation and decisions delayed while the numbers get verified by a person instead of a system.
